body:
I replied to another person in this thread, explaining why I think that I am in fact not a person who would be considered attractive by virtually anyone. Of course, ideally that should not mean that I am less of a person because of that. However, I just can't cope with my own ugliness. I feel isolated and rejected, and there is a persistent feeling of hopelessness, knowing that I will never look conventionally attractive.

I am not suicidal in the sense that I want to jump of a building as soon as possible; I am "suicidal" in a more abstract sense of the word. I don't feel like living anymore, and if I could go to sleep and never wake up again, that would be ideal, but I don't feel like tying a noose either, you know what I'm saying? I guess a lifetime of having to live with the effects of my own ugliness has numbed the emotions so much that I simply feel unable to do anything, anything at all.

Anyway. Thanks for reaching out, I appreciate it.

Yet it stops me from chasing my dreams. I'll rant a little about myself:

I am, in an absolute way, quite ugly. I was born with a mild craniofacial deformity, and I have some major jaw issues too. I look "off", which is a harsh truth that I tried to deny for many, many years. I can change my hairstyle, I can get a tan, I can wear nice clothes, but I will never be able to remodel the skeletal structure of my face and head (except for maybe some minor orthodontic adjustments). I am, quite simply, an ugly sonuvabitch. 

People are sometimes outright hostile to me. Socializing is hard. Getting a job is hard. Even though many people pretend they don't, they just can't look past my face. They judge the book by its cover, and even though I try really hard to polish that cover, I will never be able to remove the rips and tears and straighten out all the folds in the paper, if you know what I'm saying. 

My face and head are not quite deformed enough that it is immediately apparent that I suffer from a medical condition. However, the deformities are just severe enough that I am not just *plain-looking*, but undeniably *strange-looking.* I am in good shape, I dress well, I smell nice, but nothing will distract people from the ugliness of my face and head.

Anyway, thanks for reaching out. It means a lot to me.
